items.title: How timeout length determines how fast a connection pool exhausts
items.description: This applies Little's Law (average requests held in a system = arrival rate × time each one holds a connection) to the Scenario: the order service's connection pool fills with requests stuck waiting on the slow inventory call. A longer timeout means each stuck request occupies a connection longer, so the same request rate exhausts the pool with fewer requests. Drag the timeout up toward 'no timeout at all' to see why the Scenario's pool filled completely.

params.name: requestsPerSec
params.label: Requests per second hitting the slow dependency

items.compute: const poolSize = 50; const raw = params.requestsPerSec * (params.timeoutMs / 1000); const occupiedConnections = Math.min(poolSize, Math.round(raw)); return { occupiedConnections };
